normative_summary: Template v1 authoring uses Option B Canvas Focus as its information-architecture baseline.
Options A and C remain comparison prototypes only.
The comparison prototypes do not define three product modes.
Later implementation need not maintain three pages.
The fixed-physical-size Canvas continuously occupies the visual center.
Structure, node catalog, Asset, Definition, and exchange share a collapsible left navigation panel.
Properties use a collapsible right inspector.
Data, Authoritative Preview, problems, and save are invoked through a compact dock.
A selected node may expose a lightweight contextual toolbar.
The contextual toolbar triggers only the same DesignDSL editing commands and cannot create a second property fact source.
The top bar continuously shows Template identity, permanent exact StaticSchema binding, readiness or revision, and save status.
The scenario switcher is a controlled throwaway-prototype fixture for invalid, drift, binding, conflict, and preview-failure states.
The scenario switcher is not permanent author-workbench business navigation.
The Canvas provides only non-authoritative editing feedback.
Authoritative Preview is an independent action that runs the complete Evaluator and RenderEngine path.
Authoritative Preview and formal image output reuse the same Profile path.
Browser draft graphics, Asset placeholders, and LayoutTrace cannot be presented as final RenderOutput.
Ticket17 freezes workflow, information architecture, and interaction projection only.
Ticket17 adds no Template or Asset API, database, product route, or runtime semantics.
Later product visual tokens may evolve.
Visual evolution cannot break Ticket17 authority boundaries or information hierarchy.
Left navigation exposes Structure, Nodes, Assets, Definitions, and Exchange task entries in Chinese.
Structure tree, create panel, and inspector derive from the same NodeContractCatalog projection.
Asset, Definition, and Exchange panels obey their own contracts and cannot mix references, sample input, or import source into DesignDSL.
The central Canvas explicitly displays authored millimeter geometry and non-authoritative status.
Text font size is displayed in points.
DPI appears only in Authoritative Preview requests.
Stack and Grid proportional or constraint feedback is responsive only within the fixed Canvas.
The editor cannot explain DesignDSL layout with web breakpoints or CSS responsive semantics.
The right property inspector is the primary node-editing entry point.
Binding, resource, TemplateUse, Repeat, problem, and preview-detail editors open on demand rather than permanently compressing the Canvas.
Collapsing a panel changes only author view and cannot change authored values or Binding.
The bottom dock can explicitly switch navigation, properties, data, and problems and can start Authoritative Preview and save.
An INVALID Template remains editable.
An INVALID Template may be saved only after secondary confirmation.
INVALID state disables Authoritative Preview and Render.
Only a new server revalidation can restore usability after repair.
A viewport below the desktop editing threshold shows an explicit unsupported-width state.
The editor cannot compress panels into an unusable mobile editor.
The v1 prototype targets a desktop online-design workbench.
Viewport adaptation cannot alter DesignDSL physical-layout semantics.
The inspector does not expose wire or property identifiers as ordinary labels.
Each exact Property Identity projects to a dedicated Chinese label through client display metadata.
The initial property-label projection is Chinese-only and makes no localization commitment.
Display labels are not persisted into DesignDSL.
Display labels do not participate in Binding addressing and cannot become UI-only semantic aliases.
Display metadata cannot expand NodeContract.
Properties use the fixed Content, Text, Layout, Appearance, Data, Behavior, Subtemplate, and Advanced groups.
The inspector shows only groups and properties actually present in the current NodeContract.
Unknown or unconfigured property-display metadata enters a controlled Extended Properties diagnostic projection.
Unknown display metadata cannot fall back to showing wire IDs as normal author labels.
Control selection follows property type and constraints across the listed text, numeric, boolean, enum, color, picker, and read-only controls.
Numeric controls show their real millimeter or point unit and legal step and range.
Enum controls show Chinese labels while submitting exact wire values.
Every property row uses Chinese label, adaptive control, and fixed-width Binding action columns.
Long help, validation issues, and bound-source summaries appear below their property row.
Actions cannot wrap into a second row or destroy vertical alignment between controls in one group.
A static-baseline control always exists and remains editable.
Binding controls only whether evaluation overrides the authored baseline.
The UI adds no separate static-versus-bound property-mode field.
Bound state cannot be interpreted as deleting or replacing the authored baseline.
Only the global append-only BindingPolicyCatalog decides whether an exact node-kind and Property Identity can bind for the source and target types.
Chinese display metadata cannot grant bindability.
A Template cannot locally enable Binding.
An unbound property uses the outlined Chinese Bound action label.
A valid Binding uses a high-contrast filled bound-state label.
A Binding that evaluates ABSENT or ERROR uses a filled error-state label.
A redacted source summary and baseline-override explanation appear only for a bound property.
An abnormal Binding explicitly states that Authoritative Preview fails.
An abnormal Binding never implies fallback to static baseline.
The action on a property row opens the existing Binding editor.
Ordinary property lists use only Chinese display names.
The Binding editor shows exact node-local targetPropertyRef, target type, and allowed selector shape.
Exact Binding-repair semantics cannot be replaced by property display labels.
Binding mode filters current properties through the global Binding policy.
Binding mode reuses the same Chinese grouping, property rows, and status feedback.
The client cannot maintain an independent bindable-property table.
Binding mode cannot introduce Slots, nodeId links, or hidden fallback values.
The recorded prototype commit is the provenance for all three comparison layouts and their shared inspector.
Option B evidence covers the desktop workspace, panel visibility, scenario fixtures, save and preview entries, and specified property and Binding feedback.
The Web gate evidence covers 14 test files, 76 tests, and a production build.
Browser evidence covers A, B, C, a 1024-pixel desktop width, and 320, 375, 414, and 768-pixel unsupported-width states.
The recorded browser checks require no console errors or axe violations.
The specified evidence directory is the A1 local evidence location.
Temporary screenshots and inspection scripts are not specification facts and do not enter the handoff commit.
Ticket18 must reuse Option B and Ticket17 property projection.
Ticket18 cannot reopen the frozen information-architecture selection.
Ticket18 must refine Authoritative Preview, cancel, failure image removal, canonical-save resynchronization, and conflict recovery.
